questions.prompt: In the System V AMD64 ABI, what stack alignment MUST `RSP` satisfy immediately *before* executing `call func`?

options.text: 16-byte aligned (`RSP % 16 == 0`, so `RSP % 16 == 8` upon entering `func` after `call` pushes 8 bytes)

questions.prompt: What is the 128-byte Red Zone in the System V AMD64 ABI?

options.text: 128 bytes below `RSP` that leaf functions may use for locals without adjusting `RSP` (safe from signal handlers, NOT used in kernels)

questions.prompt: How does the Windows x64 ABI differ from System V AMD64 for integer arguments and caller shadow space?

options.text: Windows passes the first 4 args in `RCX, RDX, R8, R9` AND requires the caller to reserve 32 bytes of shadow space on the stack

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Position-Independent Code (PIC) on x86-64. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Required for shared libraries (`.so`/`.dll`) and ASLR-enabled PIE executables
External shared-library calls go through the PLT/GOT indirection
`mov rdi, msg` absolute 32-bit relocations always work in `-pie` shared libraries
Uses `RIP`-relative addressing (`lea rdi, [rel msg]`) instead of hardcoded absolute 64-bit addresses

questions.prompt: Match each SIMD/SSE instruction or concept to its behavior.

columns.label: Loads 128-bit aligned floats (faults `#GP` if address not 16-byte aligned)
Loads 128-bit unaligned floats safely without 16-byte alignment
Adds 4 packed 32-bit floats in parallel in one instruction

questions.prompt: Why can `cmovcc` (conditional move, e.g., `cmovg rax, rbx`) outperform a conditional branch (`jg`) on unpredictable data?

options.text: It avoids branch misprediction pipeline flushes by turning control flow into a data dependency
It works on memory destinations directly

code.source:
cmp rbx, rax
cmovg rax, rbx

questions.prompt: What does the `lock` prefix (e.g., `lock xadd [rdi], eax`) guarantee on multi-core x86 CPUs?

options.text: Makes the read-modify-write memory operation atomic across all CPU cores via cache-coherency locking

questions.prompt: What does `lock cmpxchg [rdi], rdx` implement?

options.text: Atomic Compare-And-Swap (CAS): if `[rdi] == RAX`, writes `rdx` to `[rdi]` and sets `ZF=1`; else loads `[rdi]` into `RAX` and sets `ZF=0`

questions.prompt: Under x86-64's Total Store Order (TSO) memory model, which reordering can hardware still perform without `mfence` or `lock`?

options.text: Store-Load reordering (a buffered store to `A` followed by a load from `B` can be observed out of order by another core)

questions.prompt: What is Tail-Call Optimization (TCO) in assembly?

options.text: Replacing `call target; ret` at the end of a function with `jmp target` (after restoring frame), reusing the current stack frame

questions.prompt: What does `cld` (Clear Direction Flag) ensure before `rep movsb`?

options.text: Sets `DF = 0` so `RSI` and `RDI` increment forward through memory (ABI requires `DF = 0` on function calls/returns)

questions.prompt: In GCC/Clang extended inline assembly (`asm volatile ("..." : outputs : inputs : clobbers)`), why is the clobber list critical?

options.text: It informs the compiler which registers, flags (`"cc"`), or `"memory"` the assembly modifies so the optimizer doesn't assume they are unchanged

questions.prompt: What does `rdtsc` return on x86-64?

options.text: The 64-bit Time Stamp Counter in `EDX:EAX` (cycle-level counter; pair with `lfence` or `rdtscp` to serialize execution for microbenchmarks)

questions.prompt: Select all modern binary/hardware security mitigations visible at the assembly/ELF level. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: NX / DEP (non-executable stack/heap pages, preventing shellcode execution on the stack)
Stack Canaries (`fs:0x28` guard value checked before `ret` to catch stack buffer overflows)

questions.prompt: What is Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) at the machine level?

options.text: Chaining short existing code snippets ending in `ret` ('gadgets') via forged return addresses on the stack to bypass NX

questions.prompt: What does `vzeroupper` prevent when mixing 256-bit AVX (`YMM`) code with legacy 128-bit SSE (`XMM`) code?

options.text: AVX-SSE transition penalties caused by dirty upper 128 bits of `YMM` registers

questions.prompt: Why do high-performance `memcpy` routines on modern x86 CPUs often use `rep movsb` (ERMSB / FSRM) or AVX2/AVX-512?

options.text: Modern CPUs implement Enhanced `rep movsb` in microcode at cache-line/vector speeds without manual unrolling overhead

questions.prompt: What does `prefetcht0 [rsi + 64]` hint to the CPU?

options.text: Requests fetching the cache line at `rsi + 64` into L1/all cache levels ahead of use to hide DRAM latency

questions.prompt: What is a PLT (Procedure Linkage Table) + GOT (Global Offset Table) used for in ELF dynamic linking?

options.text: Resolving calls to shared-library functions (`libc.so`) lazily or via RELRO at runtime without modifying read-only `.text`

questions.prompt: Match each x86-64 system/low-level instruction to its purpose.

columns.label: Queries processor vendor, features (SSE/AVX/BMI), and cache topology
Hints a spin-wait loop to save power and avoid memory-order pipeline clears
Guaranteed undefined opcode triggering `#UD` (used for unreachable/abort traps)

questions.prompt: Why should a spinlock loop in assembly include `pause`?

options.text: To reduce power/SMT resource contention and avoid speculative memory-order replay penalties on lock release

questions.prompt: What is the `endbr64` instruction emitted at the start of functions by modern compilers (`-fcf-protection`)?

options.text: An Intel CET Indirect Branch Tracking (IBT) landing pad marking valid targets for indirect `call`/`jmp`

questions.prompt: What does `syscall` return on Linux x86-64 when an error occurs (unlike C `libc` wrappers that set `errno`)?

options.text: A negative errno value in `RAX` between `-4095` and `-1` (e.g., `-ENOENT`)

questions.prompt: In ARM64 (AArch64) vs x86-64, how do subroutine calls store the return address?

options.text: ARM64 `BL` stores the return address in `LR` (`X30`) register rather than pushing to memory

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `XMM0`–`XMM15` in the System V AMD64 ABI. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `XMM8`–`XMM15` are callee-saved in System V AMD64 (they are ALL volatile/caller-saved in SysV, unlike Windows x64 `XMM6`–`XMM15`)
`AL` holds the count of vector registers used when calling variadic functions like `printf`

questions.prompt: When calling `printf` (a variadic function) from x86-64 Linux assembly with no floating-point arguments, what MUST you set before `call printf`?

code.source:
xor eax, eax ; 0 XMM args
call printf

questions.prompt: What does `popcnt rax, rdi` compute (BMI/SSE4.2)?

options.text: Counts the number of `1` bits (Hamming weight) in `rdi` in a single instruction

questions.prompt: What is a false dependency in x86 out-of-order execution (e.g., partial register writes like `mov al, 1` or `bsf`/`popcnt` on older CPUs)?

options.text: Writing only part of a register forces the CPU to wait on the previous value of the upper bits even when logically unrelated

questions.prompt: What does `readelf -S app` inspect in an ELF binary?

options.text: The ELF section headers (`.text`, `.rodata`, `.data`, `.bss`, `.symtab`, flags, and offsets)

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `RELRO` (Relocation Read-Only, `-Wl,-z,relro,-z,now`) in ELF binaries?

options.text: Resolves GOT entries at startup and marks the GOT read-only so attackers cannot overwrite function pointers

questions.prompt: What does `movnti [rdi], eax` (non-temporal store) do?

options.text: Writes to memory bypassing CPU caches (streaming store), avoiding cache pollution for huge write-only buffers

questions.prompt: What is macro-op fusion in modern x86-64 CPUs?

options.text: The decoder fuses `cmp`/`test` + conditional jump (`je`/`jne`) into a single internal micro-op

questions.prompt: Match each binary inspection tool to its primary output.

columns.label: Disassembles executable sections into assembly instructions
Lists defined and undefined symbols (demangled with `-C`)
Extracts printable ASCII/UTF strings embedded in the binary

questions.prompt: Why must interrupt/signal handlers NOT clobber general-purpose or `XMM` registers without saving them?

options.text: The interrupted code expects all its architectural register state to remain intact when control resumes

questions.prompt: What does `x86` `iretq` pop from the stack when returning from a 64-bit interrupt?

options.text: `RIP`, `CS`, `RFLAGS`, `RSP`, and `SS` (restoring privilege level, stack, and flags atomically)

questions.prompt: What is a branchless `abs(x)` trick for 32-bit signed `eax` in assembly?

options.text: `cdq; xor eax, edx; sub eax, edx` (uses `edx` sign mask `-1` or `0`)

code.source:
cdq
xor eax, edx
sub eax, edx

questions.prompt: Select all practices that improve performance in hand-written assembly kernels. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Minimize memory traffic by keeping accumulator values in registers
Use `loop` and `xchg [mem], reg` inside tight inner loops
Align hot loops and data buffers to 16/32/64-byte boundaries
Avoid partial-register writes that introduce false dependencies

questions.prompt: What does `default rel` at the top of a NASM 64-bit file enable?

options.text: Makes `[symbol]` memory operands default to `RIP`-relative addressing instead of 32-bit absolute

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `fs` / `gs` segment registers in 64-bit mode (where `cs`/`ds`/`es`/`ss` bases are flat 0)?

options.text: Thread-Local Storage (TLS) and OS per-CPU/TEB pointers (e.g., `fs:0x28` stack canary on Linux, `gs` on Windows/kernel)

questions.prompt: What happens if you execute a privileged instruction like `hlt` or `lgdt` in user-space (Ring 3)?

options.text: Raises a General Protection Fault (`#GP`), causing the OS to terminate the process with `SIGSEGV`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `C` ABI struct return values in System V AMD64. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Larger structs (> 16 bytes) are returned via a hidden caller-allocated pointer passed in `RDI`
Returning a struct in registers avoids heap allocation
All structs regardless of size are returned in `XMM0`
Small structs (up to 16 bytes, e.g., two `int64_t` fields) can be returned in `RAX` and `RDX`

questions.prompt: Why is writing entire large applications in assembly rarely advisable over C/C++/Rust?

options.text: Modern optimizing compilers perform global register allocation, instruction scheduling, and vectorization across huge codebases with far fewer maintenance and portability bugs
